Scope of the change: virtual timerfd in Detcore when sequentialize_threads && !recordreplay_modes.
  Product: detcore/src/fd.rs, detcore/src/syscalls/files.rs, detcore/src/syscalls/io.rs (and whatever else
  `git diff --stat 8929eeb716..dbf27d2618` shows). The round-2 claim is that scheduler.rs, scheduler/timed_waiters.rs,
  syscalls/threads.rs, tool_global.rs and tool_local.rs are byte-identical to base; verify that.
  Tests/bookkeeping: tests/backend-parity/fixtures/timerfd_semantics.c, tests/e2e/manifests/backend-parity-c.yaml,
  ci/manifest-plan/src/{timeouts.rs,runner.rs,validation_dag_static.rs,ledger/schema10/tests.rs}, scripts/validate.rs,
  regenerated ci/expected-e2e-plan.json, ci/dag/validate.json, SCORECARD.md, ci/compat-envelope/cells.json.

Things to attack specifically (not exhaustive):
  1. The new wait loop `wait_with_timerfds` in io.rs: does it rescan virtual state after EVERY host probe; can it
     spin without advancing logical time; is the guest deadline honoured in logical time; signal interruption and
     restart; the epoll paths that now ALWAYS use it for nonzero timeouts (event-stream change for epoll programs
     that watch no timerfd?); the timeout-0 and sigmask paths; interaction with maxevents, EPOLLET and ONESHOT
     consumption across retries (an edge consumed by a probe whose result is then discarded?).
  2. Deleting all scheduler timerfd bookkeeping: is there ANY program for which a timerfd wait now fails to advance
     or is misreported as deadlocked (e.g. every thread blocked in a timerfd read/poll/epoll with no other timed work)?
     Measure, do not assume.
  3. Linux fidelity vs fs/timerfd.c: create flag-before-clock order; settime order (EFAULT, EINVAL flags/timespec,
     EBADF/EINVAL fd); gettime fd-before-EFAULT; read/readv/preadv2 EINVAL for short total length (consumes nothing),
     consume-then-EFAULT, scatter across iovecs, EAGAIN, ERESTARTSYS; pread ESPIPE; epoll ET/ONESHOT/maxevents; select
     count and remaining timeout; poll merge.
  4. The four rescue findings claimed fixed: realtime ABSTIME, select count, invalid timespec, lifecycle cleanup.
  5. Mode gate: record/replay and non-sequentialized runs must be byte-for-byte the old host-passthrough behaviour.
  6. Bookkeeping: detcore_unit ratchet now 755 (was 760 at abcebadd40, 748 at base) must equal the measured
     `cargo test -p hermit-detcore --lib` count; 856->858 / 852->854 / NON_CI 173->172 unchanged from round 1;
     no selector/command/comparator/timeout relaxed; expected-plan delta exactly the two cells.
  7. The fixture change to `abstime_past` (now polls before reading) — is this a legitimate native-fidelity fix or a
     weakened assertion? Run the fixture natively yourself several times.
  8. Required markers present: `// AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED` at new dispatch entries and
     `// TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-3229)` at determinization blocks.
  9. Every number in the PR description's Validation section and review-findings list: reproduce what you can.

> GOALPOST-MOVING REVIEW RULE
>
> Adversarial reviewers must look explicitly for goalpost moving. We are extremely skeptical of any goalpost moving. YOU DO NOT CLEAR THE BAR BY SIMPLY LOWERING THE BAR.
>
> Treat each of these as an explicit review target:
> - weakening an assertion so a test passes
> - widening a tolerance · adding an exemption · skipping a case · relaxing a comparator
> - renaming or relabelling so a failure reads as a pass
> - deleting a check rather than satisfying it

Compare every changed test, threshold, allowlist, skip, label, classification, and gate with the base revision.
Determine whether the implementation now meets the original requirement or whether the requirement was changed
to admit the implementation. Call out either result explicitly, including when no lowering of the bar is present.
The round-2 commit deletes 5 unit tests together with the scheduler code they tested; judge whether that is
"deleting a check rather than satisfying it" or the legitimate removal of tests for removed code.

Review method: trace behaviour through the real execution path; check evidence against what it claims to prove;
inspect production and test changes together; give concrete file:line findings with impact and required change.
